The three vocabulary lists already agreed, so no gateway, BFF or SPA list needed changing. I wrote no DB-backed test; the new store_proofs rows name the existing #[ignore] DB tests, which I did not run. No docker, commit, push, stash or rustfmt.

1. Gateway pre-consume guard (`gateway_consume_violations`, test `the_gateway_pre_consumes_once_spends_only_and_consumes_and_launches_in_one_detached_task`):
   - Exactly one `ConsumeApprovalRequest` literal in the whole gateway, inside `preconsume_request`, and every mention of `omit_call` is `omit_call: true`.
   - One `.consume_approval(` call, inside `impl ApprovalConsumer for GrpcApprovalConsumer` and inside `consume_within_bound`. Only `.consumed` is read from the answer. No `.tool_input_json`, `.tool_name`, `.authority`, `.step_id`, `.same_claim` or `.already_consumed` in the flow.
   - Exactly one `tokio::spawn(`, in `spawn_consume_then_launch`; none in the other pre-consume functions or in `continue_run`.
   - `trait ApprovalConsumer` declares `Send + Sync`. The Sync-less variant is a compile mutation (`spawn_consume_then_launch` stops building with E0277), described in a comment; the in-memory mutation only proves the guard names the supertraits.
   - `continue_run` reads the switch once, builds one launch closure, returns `Ok(launch())` with the switch off, and only then calls `spawn_consume_then_launch(`.
   - The one `AgentResume` literal names only mode, approval_id, claim_token, brief and segment_no.
2. Spend gate and refusal arms (`spend_gate_violations` and `refusal_arm_violations` (c2), one test):
   - The spent arm is guarded by `spend.is_spent()` alone, comes before the confirmed arm, and never terminalizes.
   - The request-construction failure checks `spend.is_spent()` before it terminalizes.
   - `SpentByGateway` is named only in the builders of the spend.
   - The two callers of `agentic_run_stream` state `ApprovalSpend::NotSpent` and `approval_spend_for(resume_enabled)`.
   - Three `dispatch_unknown_event(spend,` sites and one `connected_payload(.., spend)`.
   - The five arms keep the order spent, confirmed, typed, unreachable, final. The typed arm is guarded by `continuing` and `!spend.is_spent()` and contains no terminalize, `RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED`, `approval_spent` or `SpentByGateway`.
3. Closed vocabulary (`continue_vocabulary_violations`, test `every_refusal_the_executor_can_send_is_in_the_gateways_closed_vocabulary`):
   - Every carrier-code literal on the executor's resume path, and every word of the `Refusal` enum in resume.rs, is in the gateway's lists.
   - Every token is sent by some executor or session-core production code.
   - The frame list equals the 17 message tokens plus the five derived and gateway-made codes.
   - This confirmed the executor-sourced list is complete: all 17 tokens are present. `in_place_seed_invalid` is Internal, so it is not a refusal and classifies as unknown.
4. Coupled flip (test `the_gateway_and_the_executor_flip_together_the_replay_rule_the_one_reader_no_attestation`):
   - `resume_pair_violations`: every `.same_claim` read in the executor is followed by `&& replay_is_fenced`, and `replay_is_fenced` is bound once to `ledger_enabled()`.
   - `gateway_resume_reader_violations`: `loop_resume_enabled()` is called exactly once in the gateway, inside `continue_run`; the gateway never names the env var or `LOOP_RESUME_ENV`; `switch_table()` has model-gateway and execution-core rows for the switch.
   - `no_attestation_violations`: no `consumed_by_gateway` in Rust production sources under the guard's source trees or in non-comment proto lines.
5. Writer-gate guard (`writer_gate_argument_violations`, test `a_delegated_child_never_writes_a_fold_and_the_gate_is_handed_the_depth_and_the_release`):
   - `run_rounds` calls `writer_gate(req, &ctx.route, ctx.effect_ledger, ctx.depth, ctx.release.is_some(), in_place)` in exactly that shape.
   - A child context is built from `depth: parent.depth + 1`.
   - `decide` still refuses `self.depth > 0`.
   - The mutation proof (a literal `0` depth) turns the guard red.
6. `store_proofs` rows: the Continue row gains 9 tests (5 in sse.rs, 4 in `tests/continue_preconsume_test.rs`); the Consume row gains 6 (session-core omit_call, renewal and terminalization). Seven of the new rows have rename or comment-out mutation proofs.
7. Compose: the gateway line `EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED: ${...:-false}` already existed and `switch_table()` already pinned it, so I only verified it. One stale comment sentence was corrected (see deviations).
8. BFF parity (`tests/continue_error_vocabulary.rs`):
   - New test: the BFF list is a subset of the gateway's `CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS` with equal statuses, and the difference is exactly `continue_incomplete` and `missing_bearer`.
   - New test: the SPA's `CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS` equals the gateway's `CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS`, in order, 22 tokens.
   - The model-gateway source is read only as a test. No SPA, BFF or gateway list changed.

S7c-B1 (step 8) is built and verified. continue_run now pre-consumes the approval when EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED is on at the gateway, and agentic_run_stream classifies dispatch failures by the gateway's own spend knowledge. What changed in sse.rs (production):
- continue_resume(approval_id, claim_token, mode: &'static str) is still the one AgentResume literal. It now writes mode: mode.to_owned(), segment_no 0, and nothing else.
- continue_run reads loop_resume_enabled() once, after continue_preflight, and picks the stage with resume_mode_for(resume_enabled, detail.resumable).
  - It builds the consumer and the spend-only request from clones, before the launch closure takes ownership.
  - The one 'static launch closure holds the single agentic_run_stream call. approval_spend_for(resume_enabled) is evaluated inside it, so the spent state is claimed only when the closure runs.
  - Switch off: return Ok(launch()), no consume, no spawn, segment mode, NotSpent.
  - Switch on: spawn_consume_then_launch(..).await. Closed(status, code) becomes continue_error, Status(st) becomes grpc_status_to_http, and a vanished task becomes 503 continue_unavailable.
- agentic_run_stream gained a trailing spend: ApprovalSpend parameter, and invoke_stream_sse passes NotSpent. It computes continuing before the resume moves and builds the first frame through connected_payload.
- The three agent_dispatch_unavailable sites now call dispatch_unknown_event(spend, ..).
- A request-construction failure after a spend sends continue_refused and does not terminalize.
- Arm order for Ok(Ok(Err(status))):
  - spent arm: guarded by spend.is_spent(), uses classify and continue_failure_event, publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED only for Unreachable and Unknown, never terminalizes.
  - the committed confirmed-rejection arm, unchanged.
  - the new typed-refusal arm: guarded by continuing, not spent, and classify returning Refused. It sends continue_refusal_event with no approval_spent, no RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED, no terminalization.
  - the committed unreachable arm.
  - the committed final arm.
- The five review findings from the pure-pieces round:
  - (1) classify_continue_dispatch_failure's doc now says it is spend-agnostic and why the arm order matters. Tests pin both regimes.
  - (2) the spend is claimed only inside the closure, scan-guarded.
  - (3) a zero-retention trailer on the consume keeps its typed body (see deviation 1).
  - (4) the 10 s bound is tested through the real GrpcApprovalConsumer::consume (a paused-clock test over a real transport with a never-answering server), plus a scan that the impl contains consume_within_bound(client.consume_approval(.
  - (5) the same-token race runs over the real transport against a single-use server that gives the real replay answer shape (consumed false, already_consumed true, same_claim true, with the call only when it was not omitted). The doubles in the integration file use the same shape.
  - (6) the claim token is never logged, scan-guarded.
- #[allow(dead_code)] was removed from everything now wired. CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS is now read by a debug_assert in continue_error.
- The doc comments of continue_run, continue_resume and the block header were updated.

Tests:
- Unit tests in continue_run_tests: a hung session-core through the real consumer, the bound scan, the same-token and distinct-token race over a real transport, the ZDR trailer on the consume, the off-switch byte-identity of the request, continue_resume's stage, the order and shape scan of continue_run, the spent-state-in-closure scan, the arm-order scan, the stream's ambiguous and connected frames, and the claim-token log scan.
- The three existing tests that needed the new arity were updated, with no assertion weakened. A re-grep found no test expecting agent_dispatch_unavailable on a FailedPrecondition path.
- Integration file tests/continue_preconsume_test.rs:

  - switch off: no consume and a byte-identical connected payload;
  - a lost consume (another claim, or the same token) is a 409 with zero RunAgent;
  - refused consumes map to their closed codes with no upstream message;
  - two simultaneous same-token clicks give one dispatch;
  - the full frame table, 17 cases across switch on and off, covering FailedPrecondition, Aborted, NotFound, InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied, DeadlineExceeded, an unlisted refusal, unreachable and dropped, with frame code, approval_spent, RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and terminalization checked;

### WS03 S7b hardening (2026-10-18): recorded decisions

(a) Fence failures after a won claim are a refusal, not a fallback. Once the in-place resume has claimed the fold, a deterministic failure of the fence save (ContentRefused, StoreOff, InvalidArgument; also Unavailable, Stale and Closed) ends the request with the closed token resume_checkpoint_unavailable. A denial stays resume_forbidden and a ZDR trailer stays the catalogue refusal (fence_refusal). Nothing of the restored round has run. Why not a fallback to stage 1: the claim has already made the fold `resuming` and the consume has spent the click, and a stage-1 segment that ran now would be a second, unfenced continuation of the same pause. The fence is the only thing that lets exactly one claimant dispatch. A deterministic failure (a content refusal, a store switched off, an invalid argument) would fail again for any other claimant, so refusing is honest and retrying cannot help. The cost is a spent click and a stranded `resuming` fold, which the renewed recovery window (D9) and the lease expiry handle. A fallback is taken only BEFORE the claim (the writer-off decision, in_place_writer_off) or for failures the design lists as post-claim fold or ledger unreadability (FoldUnreadable, check_fold failures, LedgerUnavailable, PausedStepUnsettled, LedgerIdentityMismatch), where nothing has been dispatched and D3 leaves the fold alone.

(b) Stage 1 and an ambiguous release pre-reserve. In stage 1 a release pre-reserve that fails, or whose answer is lost, holds the release back (it is not run, whatever its class) and lets the loop go on. The earlier claim that the at-most-one-model-loop-per-approval invariant holds for a read release too is true only when the pre-reserve answered. What bounds it: the consume has a single winner (another claim token is refused with continuation_already_consumed); a same-claim replay is accepted only with the effect ledger on; a second loop needs the same client-chosen claim token twice AND the reserve failing or being lost both times; the released call itself is run by neither; and with the ledger on the later rounds of two loops of one segment compute the same step ids, so an effect of the second loop should meet the first loop's row (AlreadyReserved) and be closed unknown_outcome, not run twice. What does NOT bound it: the duplicated inference rounds, their cost and any duplicated read calls or assistant messages; and the post-claim fallback path (D3), where a lapsed 120 s lease lets a same-claim retry claim the OLD pause again and run it beside or after a stage-1 loop that has moved the run on (reconcile L1 refuses only when the release row exists, and stage 1 holds no row after an ambiguous reserve). The gateway's 409-first rule (D1) makes this hard to reach through the gateway; a non-gateway same-claim caller can reach it. The in-place stage does not have the window: it ends with resume_checkpoint_unavailable and dispatches nothing. Follow-up, not built: end the stage-1 request without running further rounds after an ambiguous pre-reserve, as the in-place stage already does, which would make INV-02 hold whatever the ledger answers. It would change stage-1 behaviour with the switches on, so it needs its own decision.

(c) A deliberate, log-only change. With AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED on and every S7 switch off, a continuation (a `segment` request included) logs one content-free info line, loop_resume_stage {run_id, resume_stage: stage_one, fallback_reason: ""}; a `loop` request also logs loop_resume_downgraded before the consume (and still logs it when the consume then refuses). Runtime results are unchanged. With every switch off, continue included, grpc.rs refuses continue_disabled first and no line is reached, so the byte-identical rule holds for the shipped defaults. The earlier statement that the only reachable difference was one warn line is superseded by this one.

O1 (observation, not decided). A pinned or waived stage-1 continuation never reaches its release: the synthetic seed round carries no provider_used or model_used, and ModelRoute::verify_response stops the run subscription_route_unavailable before the first dispatch. It is unreachable today, since a waived or pinned run is never offered a loop approval (the pause site makes it cold), and a continue for one is downgraded or refused. If pinned continuations are ever enabled, the seed needs the route's own provider and model.

(b) Stage 1 and an ambiguous release pre-reserve (CORRECTED 2026-10-18; INV-02 gap OPEN).
